limits: Proves an explicitly enabled finish caller refuses to start gate work when its supervisor refuses, and still runs the old green gate when granted. Fake coordinator, no service/DB/network: actual Kyle CLI renewal, watchdog process-tree stopping and authority authorization are not established here. The historical gate ignores the rollout signal and runs work after refusal; the same fixture gives it a clean good run. Off-path, metadata, credential isolation and nested invocation are separately covered by focused regression tests. A planted garbage flag must stay on the old path even with a refusing supervisor configured. bad-unavailable (issue #1678): a coordinator that never answers unless the caller bounded the wait with --wait must end in the named 'coordination unavailable: <code>' fail inside the bound; a caller that passes no --wait hangs past the runner's timeout and reads GOOD (the miss), as does one that ends without the name. The fake models kyle-lock's --wait contract as read from kyle 4aa3a2aa, not a live client.

anchors.why: Unmodified pre-opt-in caller; it starts the gate despite a refused supervisor and agrees on the green fixture.
